items.text: Beacon defines a required execution host surface contract for execution-bound features, including `execution/index.md`, `execution/architecture-blueprint.md`, delivery baseline, git workflow, and technical review contract.
Beacon blocks `implement` when architecture blueprint projection is missing, drifted, or not bound to the canonical execution host.
Beacon treats branch / service / worktree facts as explicit frozen facts, not as acceptable silent defaults.

Beacon marks `source=version_default`, `source=project_config_seed`, blank `approved_by`, blank `reviewed_at`, or missing managed projection as weak fact sources that cannot unlock implementation by themselves.
Beacon provides a per-subskill material effect registry covering host, truth, execution, gate, support, toolkit, compatibility, and project-local skills.

Beacon requires every human-facing subskill invocation to resolve to `writeback_completed`, `writeback_required`, `obligation_opened`, `truth_reopen_required`, `execution_host_update_required`, `evidence_update_required`, or `read_only_route_only`.
Beacon converts accepted support findings into explicit material updates, release blockers, or `artifact_update_obligations`.
Beacon keeps support surfaces advisory unless their findings are adopted through `change`, truth surfaces, execution host updates, evidence updates, or obligations.

Beacon makes `beacon-toolkit-branch-governance` write delivery service, branch, and worktree updates through canonical git workflow, technical review contract, execution host, service slice, and metadata surfaces.
Beacon blocks QA and release while blocking artifact update obligations remain open.
Beacon emits diagnostics that name the missing material, default-seeded field, unadopted support finding, open obligation, and recommended repair surface.
Beacon preserves the main lifecycle boundary and does not turn support or toolkit skills into truth sources, gate sources, or new lifecycle stages.
Implement current frozen revision
